page: Vultr vcg-l40s-16c-180g-48vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with an Intel Xeon 6448H processor featuring 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs on an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared allocation model and lacks hyperthreading. System memory totals 180.0 GB, providing 11.25 GB of RAM per core. For hardware acceleration, the server includes a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 1200 GB NVMe SSD.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in LLM inference workloads. For a small 135M model, prompt processing reaches 13631.52 tokens per second, and text generation achieves 610.8 tokens per second. With a medium 7B model, prompt processing registers at 6293.73 tokens per second, and text generation reaches 153.1 tokens per second, placing these metrics in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also ranks in the top 10% at 15.59 GB/sec. Standard CPU and memory benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core (34834.61) and Passmark CPU score (40930.36), fall within the average middle 50% range.

The server offers high resource density with its 11.25:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and a substantial 48 GB VRAM buffer, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive GPU workloads that do not require dedicated CPU allocations. However, the shared CPU allocation model and the lack of hyperthreading represent a potential tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, exclusive CPU compute. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is relatively low at 66.7 GB/sec compared to the read-only small block bandwidth of 2801.1 GB/sec.

This configuration is suited for medium-scale LLM inference, data science pipelines, and GPU-accelerated database operations. The combination of 180 GB of system memory, 1200 GB of NVMe storage, and the NVIDIA L40S GPU supports workloads such as transformer-based model serving, batch text processing, and memory-heavy analytical tasks.
